attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No explicit generator is known whose H_N beats unrestricted N^{1+epsilon} circuits while also defeating range-label imbalance, promise solvers on U_N, and semantic block-cover compression.
steps: Fix N and let K^+=|U_N^+|, K^-=|U_N^-|.
If K^+<=K^-, build a membership circuit Pos_N(y)=OR_{z in U_N^+}[y=z] of size O(K^+ L). Then H_N(x)=OR_j Pos_N(G_{N,j}(x)) on every x.
If K^-<K^+, build Neg_N(y)=OR_{z in U_N^-}[y=z] of size O(K^- L). Then H_N(x)=NOT AND_j Neg_N(G_{N,j}(x)), since every generated query lies in U_N.
Composing either membership circuit with the charged all-query generator gives C(H_N)<=C(G_N)+O(M L min{K^+,K^-})+O(M).
With M=N^{q+o(1)}, L=N^{o(1)}, and C(G_N)<=N^{rho+o(1)}, any claimed C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} lower bound with rho<1+epsilon forces min{K^+,K^-}>N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)}.

The target substitution calculation is unchanged: if SAT has size n^c circuits, composing those circuits with G_N gives C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)}, contradicting the source lower bound when max{rho,q}<1+epsilon.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The argument proves conditional bridge and falsifier lemmas. It does not prove the required source lower bound for H_N, so it does not prove P != NP or NP notin P/poly.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-magnification bridge realization: generated-OR range-balance gate

assumptions: Source lower-bound model is unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuit size for H_N, not a restricted Gamma model.
The generator outputs all M queries with total circuit size N^{rho+o(1)}; if only per-query generation is available, the rho term must be replaced by the charged total generation cost.
The route claims only a bridge: proving the source lower bound is a separate non-natural lower-bound obligation.
definitions: source object: the explicit Boolean function family H_N on N input bits defined by a generated OR of SAT queries, H_N(x)=OR_{j<=N^{q+o(1)}} SAT(G_{N,j}(x)).
target object: SAT on L=(log N)^d bit encodings, with the target consequence SAT notin P/poly if the bridge preserves every polynomial SAT exponent.

controlled interface: a nonblackbox compact all-query generator G_N of circuit size N^{rho+o(1)} producing M=N^{q+o(1)} SAT instances of length L, with every generation and membership-test cost charged to H_N.

target-preserving condition: max{q,rho}<1+epsilon, L=(log N)^d with d>1 or otherwise lookup-safe, and no nonuniform advice about SAT beyond either a hypothesized target circuit or an explicitly charged promise/range solver.

equations.label: carrier_definition

equations.label: range_balance_upper_bound

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If min{|U_N^+|,|U_N^-|}<=N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)}, the proposed source lower bound is false in the intended model, so the route must repair the generator or quarantine this carrier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Adds a concrete source-side falsifier to the generated-OR magnification bridge: low satisfiable or low unsatisfiable support in the actual generated range gives a subthreshold H_N circuit.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Range-label balance is a necessary source condition for the generated-OR carrier. For H_N(x)=OR_{j<=M} SAT(G_{N,j}(x)), M=N^{q+o(1)}, L=(log N)^d, and an all-query generator of size N^{rho+o(1)}, if U_N is the generated formula range and U_N^+,U_N^- are its satisfiable and unsatisfiable parts, then H_N has circuits of size N^{rho+o(1)}+N^{q+o(1)} min{|U_N^+|,|U_N^-|}. Hence a valid N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound with rho<1+epsilon forces min{|U_N^+|,|U_N^-|}>N^{1+epsilon-q-o(1)}.

assumptions: The lower bound for H_N holds for infinitely many or all relevant N as needed by the target separation quantifier.
For every fixed c, L^c=N^{o(1)}.
The source lower bound survives the range-balance, promise-solver, and semantic block-cover upper-bound audits.
definitions: C(H_N) denotes nonuniform circuit complexity of the N-bit carrier function.
SAT notin P/poly means no polynomial-size nonuniform circuits decide SAT on all input lengths.
Target-clean means the construction of H_N is fixed independently of a guessed SAT circuit and all nonuniform information used to evaluate generated queries is charged.

definitions: A semantic block partition groups query positions and replaces singleton SAT evaluation by a nonuniform circuit for the OR of SAT over that block's actual generated tuple range.
A promise SAT solver on U_N is any circuit correct on U_N, arbitrary off U_N, and charged by its size in the carrier upper bound.
A route is viable only as a bridge candidate, not as evidence that P != NP has been proved.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The argument does not naturalize one-sided signed high-threshold PTFs, nor any degree omega(log N) object whose density bound becomes superpolynomially small.
steps: Type the proposed proof object as p:{-1,1}^N -> R with degree d, mean zero, variance sigma^2, and uniform poly(N) evaluation.
Let Y be a uniform random truth table and set Z=p(Y)^2.
By Boolean hypercontractivity, E[p(Y)^4] <= 9^d sigma^4.
Apply Paley-Zygmund to Z with lambda=1/4 to obtain Pr[|p(Y)|>=sigma/2] >= (9/16)9^{-d}.
If theta<=sigma/2, then R_p={|p|>=theta} has at least this density.
The assumed separation makes R_p accept SAT_m and reject every SIZE(m^k) truth table, so it is useful against the target class.
When d=O(log N), the density is N^{-O(1)}; with poly(N) constructivity this is a natural property and a PRF falsifier in the usual full-truth-table sense.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-level barrier certificate, not evidence for P != NP. It says a normalized absolute low-degree separator would collide with natural-proof barriers; it does not construct a SAT lower bound.

assumptions: Truth tables are encoded as {-1,1}^N and N=2^m.
p has zero uniform mean and nonzero variance sigma^2=E[p(Y)^2].
The coefficient description or evaluator of p is uniform and runs in poly(N), with no SAT truth-table advice.
Usefulness is absolute: all SIZE(m^k) truth tables have |p| below theta while SAT_m has |p| at least theta.
definitions: source object: a poly(N)-evaluable real multilinear polynomial p on the N=2^m truth-table bits of SAT_m, with degree d, mean 0, L2 norm sigma, and claimed absolute separation.
target object: the Razborov-Rudich natural property R_p={y in {-1,1}^N: |p(y)| >= theta} useful against SIZE(m^k).
controlled interface: the hypercontractive L4/L2 tail lower bound converts normalized absolute deviation into largeness while preserving the same truth-table coordinates.
target-preserving condition: p has a uniform poly(N)-time evaluator, theta <= sigma/2, SAT_m is accepted, and every size m^k circuit truth table has |p| < theta.
largeness parameter: density at least (9/16)9^{-d}, hence polynomial when d=O(log N).
barrier type: natural-proof barrier applies if pseudorandom functions exist in the target circuit size range.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No construction is known for a short, cap-aware, advice-free verifier whose accepted set is universally hard or whose uniform selector is proved to choose only hard accepted tables.
steps: Fix a kappa-dense source length set M and a uniform selector S that outputs an accepted certificate c_m for each m in M.
Let T_m be the emitted m-bit truth table selected by S, and assume C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m}.
For each target length n choose the largest or canonical m in M with m<=n<=kappa m.
Define L_n(x_1,...,x_n)=T_m(x_1,...,x_m), ignoring the remaining n-m bits.
Uniformity: compute m, run S and V to obtain or stream T_m, then answer the indexed bit in 2^{O(n)} time because m<=n.

Lower bound: a circuit for L_n of size 2^{delta n} yields, by fixing ignored variables, a circuit for T_m of comparable size. For delta<epsilon/kappa this contradicts C(T_m)>2^{epsilon m} for large n.
Tried to weaken SelectorHard to ExistsHard, but V^+ with an early all-zero certificate preserves ExistsHard and makes canonical selection easy, so the weakening is invalid.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The bridge is valid route-level progress, but it assumes the central source soundness property. It does not construct the MCSP carrier and does not prove P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: MCSP carrier transfer with selector-soundness audit

assumptions: There is an infinite cofinal set M of source lengths such that for every large n there is m in M with m<=n<=kappa m.
For each m in M, S(1^m) outputs c_m accepted by V_m within 2^{O(m)} time.
The selected table T_m=T_{m,c_m} has Boolean circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}.
The selector and verifier do not use nonuniform advice depending on the target length.
The verifier profile satisfies epsilon<=alpha_V, where alpha_V is the best known block-checkpoint upper-bound cap for emitted tables.
definitions: source object: A deterministic verifier-emitter V_m taking O(m)-bit certificates c, running in 2^{O(m)} time, and either rejecting or emitting a truth table T_{m,c} in {0,1}^{2^m}.
target object: A language L in E with C_n(L_n)>2^{delta n} for all large n, obtained by padding selected m-bit truth tables to nearby input lengths.

controlled interface: A uniform E-time selector S which, on input 1^m, returns an accepted certificate c_m, with C(T_{m,c_m})>2^{epsilon m}; universal soundness is the special case where every accepted certificate has this property.

target-preserving condition: The source lengths are kappa-dense, the selector is uniform and advice-free, epsilon is below the verifier checkpoint cap alpha_V, and padding preserves the lower-bound exponent delta<epsilon/kappa.

equations.label: density_window
equations.valid_when: Valid when source lengths form a named kappa-dense sequence covering all sufficiently large target lengths.

equations.label: source_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the selected accepted certificate is sound for MCSP no-side threshold 2^{epsilon m}.

equations.label: padding_transfer
equations.valid_when: Applies after prefix padding preserves circuits from target length n back to source length m.

equations.label: canonicalization_budget
equations.valid_when: Requires short certificates and uniform exhaustive or direct selection within the E-time construction budget.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If one accepted easy table can be selected at any large source length, the derived L may have small circuits there, so the route-level lower-bound transfer is invalid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Positive bridge lemma replacing existential carrier hardness by selector-sound hardness; it preserves the earlier quantitative delta<epsilon/kappa transfer.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A short MCSP carrier transfers to an E circuit lower bound only through universal no-side soundness or through a uniform selector whose chosen accepted table is hard on every source length. Existential hard witnesses inside a contaminated accepted set are not a target-preserving source condition.

assumptions: The certificate ordering or selector rule is part of the explicit construction.
The added all-zero certificate has O(m) length and verification time 2^{O(m)}.
No external promise forbids contaminated easy certificates.
definitions: V^+_m(0^{a m}) emits the all-zero table and accepts; on other certificates it simulates V_m.
The property ExistsHard_m: there exists an accepted c with C(T_{m,c})>2^{epsilon m} is preserved by V -> V^+.
The property SelectorHard_m(S): C(T_{m,S(1^m)})>2^{epsilon m} is generally not preserved.

equations.latex: \exists c\ C(T_{m,c})>2^{\epsilon m}\ \Rightarrow\ \exists c\ C(T^+_{m,c})>2^{\epsilon m}
equations.valid_when: Valid when V plus accepts all original hard certificates and adds only extra easy certificates.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Negative bridge lemma certifying that an existential MCSP carrier is not target-preserving without universal soundness or a hard selector.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Existential hard acceptance is not invariant under easy contamination: for any verifier V with at least one hard accepted certificate, V^+ that also accepts a distinguished certificate emitting 0^{2^m} preserves the existential claim but destroys every canonical selector that chooses the first accepted certificate.

assumptions: The circuit model has at least fan-in two Boolean gates over m inputs, so the number of size-s circuits is 2^{Theta(s log s)}.
No succinct lower-bound certificate is supplied to replace brute-force circuit enumeration.
definitions: Postfilter means enumerate circuits of size at most s_m and compare each against a candidate truth table before selecting it.
The target construction budget for truth-table production at source length m is 2^{O(m)}.
Constant threshold means s_m=2^{epsilon m} for fixed epsilon>0.

equations.valid_when: Valid when counting ordinary Boolean circuits of size s_m over m input variables.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Quarantines a tempting repair: hardness must be certified by the source verifier or selector, not discovered by E-time MCSP filtering.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A uniform E construction cannot repair contamination by postfiltering accepted tables with a brute-force MCSP test at constant threshold 2^{epsilon m}; the test costs about 2^{2^{epsilon m+o(m)}} on m-bit truth tables.

control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a named verifier family with O(m)-bit certificates, kappa-dense lengths, epsilon<=alpha_V, and universal or selector soundness is proved without circular circuit lower-bound assumptions.

Extraction is valid with a uniform hard selector or universal no-side soundness and gives delta<epsilon/kappa.
Selector, verifier, length map, and padding must be uniform E-time and advice-free.
Needed to block easy-contamination and make the carrier target-preserving.
Brute-force MCSP filtering at constant threshold violates the E budget.

selector advice leakage: a nonuniform selector can hide the hard witness and yields only a nonuniform consequence
MCSP postfilter falsifier: brute-force filtering at threshold 2^{epsilon m} exceeds the E construction budget
checkpoint-cap falsifier: any claimed threshold epsilon>alpha_V is contradicted by the verifier block-simulation upper bound

gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A formal proof that the chosen uniform selector always returns a table with C(T)>2^{epsilon m}, or a universal soundness theorem for every accepted certificate; without this certificate the intuition is not valid for the proof queue.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: contamination_rank r, the position of z_m in the canonical certificate order or in the selector's search priority

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 23 proves the exact selector quantifier needed by the MCSP carrier route. The valid transfer is not from existence of a hard accepted certificate, but from universal hardness of accepted certificates or from a uniform selector certified to choose a hard one. Easy contamination is a concrete falsifier for weaker source claims, and brute-force MCSP postfiltering cannot repair it within E.
